Gavaya : m: A monkey-chief (vānarendra, kapiśreṣṭha).

Of great prowess (mahāvīrya), he came to Rāma with a hundred crores of monkeys 3. 267. 3, 1.

Gavākṣa : m.: A monkey-chief (kapiśreṣṭha) with a tail like that of a cow (golāṅgūla).

He brought with him to Rāma sixty thousand crores of monkeys 3. 267. 4, 1; he was eaten up by Kumbhakarṇa 3. 271. 4.

Gavāṁ tīrtham : nt.: Name of a tīrtha.

One of the holy tīrthas on the river Gomatī 3. 93. 2; the Pāṇḍavas, having bathed there, gave as gifts cows and wealth; they satisfied gods, manes and the Brāhmaṇas at this tīrtha 3. 9

.
